When node1 has no direct path to the output, the skip edge restores connectivity and gives much larger gains (exps 17,18).
Replacing the residual skip with a conv removes the identity path and hurts, while filling an empty e3 helps strongly (exps 73,74 vs 71,72,76).
With e5 absent, e4 is a critical output path, so adding a conv there yields huge gains (exps 36,37).
Removing e5 when e4 is already none leaves the output with few or no paths, causing large drops (exps 54,55).
Without the e3 skip, the conv path through e5 matters more, so deleting it hurts more (exps 52,55,57,59 vs 51,56,58).
Adding a 3x3 conv to a cell otherwise built from weak 1x1 convs adds missing receptive field (exps 27-29 vs 21-26).
Replacing a parameter-free skip on the final edge with conv3x3 yields bigger gains than replacing none or avg_pool (exps 8,9 vs 1-7).

Replacing the node1-to-output skip removes a residual path, which helps less or hurts compared with filling an empty e4 (exps 34,40 vs 31,36-38).

raw:
Each hypothesis below rests on the 100 experiments. The common thread is connectivity. Node 3 is the sum of e3(x0), e4(x1) and e5(x2). When an edit restores the only path to the output, or cuts it, the change is very large, around 20–78 pp. Otherwise, adding convolutions helps most in weak or all-1x1 cells and helps little or hurts in strong conv3x3 cells that already have a skip.

1. **e3→skip_connect when e3=none: higher.** Filling an empty input-to-output edge gained +3–74 pp (exps 11, 12, 16–18). Replacing a conv or pool there gained only about +1–5 pp (exps 13–15). Caveat: in the all-skip and all-pool cells (exps 19, 20) the same edit lost 17–29 pp.
2. **e3→skip_connect when e4=none: higher.** When x1 has no direct route to the output, the skip adds a missing path (exps 17, 18).
3. **e3→nor_conv_3x3 when e3=skip_connect: lower.** Swapping out an existing skip lost 0.6–5 pp (exps 73, 74). Filling an empty e3 gained much more (exps 71, 72, 76, 78, 79).
4. **e4→nor_conv_3x3 when e5=none: higher.** The new conv restores, or strongly adds, an output path (exps 36, 37).
5. **e5→none when e4=none: lower.** Removing e5 then leaves the output with few or no paths. Losses were 7–76 pp (exps 54, 55).
6. **e5→none when e3=none: lower.** Without the skip, removing the conv on x2 hurts more (exps 52, 55, 57, 59).
7. **e0→nor_conv_3x3 when e1=nor_conv_1x1: higher.** Adding conv3x3 depth to weak 1x1 cells gained about +3/+4/+7 pp (exps 27–29). In conv3x3 cells the gain was about 0–3 pp.
8. **e5→nor_conv_3x3 when e5=skip_connect: higher.** Replacing a parameter-free skip with conv3x3 gained a lot (exps 8, 9). Replacing none or avg_pool gained less (exps 1–7).
9. **e5→avg_pool_3x3 when e5=none: higher.** Replacing nothing with a pool is mildly positive (exps 94, 96). Replacing a conv with a pool hurts (exps 91, 93, 95, 100).
10. **e4→nor_conv_3x3 when e4=skip_connect: lower.** Losing the x1→output skip removes a residual path. Results ranged from about +0.6 pp to −9 pp (exps 34, 40).
